Display conditional effects of predictors for mvgam models

Source: R/conditional_effects.mvgam.R
conditional_effects.mvgam.Rd

Plot the conditional effects of one or more numeric / categorical predictors in fitted mvgam models, including up-to-three-way interactions. A thin wrapper around marginaleffects::plot_predictions() that auto-enumerates the model's term labels (across both observation and trend submodels) and produces one ggplot per term.

as.data.frame.mvgam_conditional_effects() returns the underlying prediction grid as a long-format data.frame (one row per grid point, per effect, per response). Columns are resp (present only when the fit is multivariate), effect (the primary conditioning variable name), estimate__, lower__, upper__, followed by whichever additional grid columns marginaleffects populated. The three estimate columns take brms's names, as in the frame conditional_smooths.mvgam() returns.

Use this to reach the raw numbers when you want to build a custom plot, overlay several fits, or compare against a known truth. It removes the need to know whether the fit was univariate or multivariate before extracting.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'mvgam'
conditional_effects(
  x,
  effects = NULL,
  type = "expected",
  points = FALSE,
  rug = FALSE,
  process_error = FALSE,
  series = NULL,
  resp = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'mvgam_conditional_effects'
plot(x, plot = TRUE, ask = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mvgam_conditional_effects'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mvgam_conditional_effects'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

x

An object of class mvgam_conditional_effects.

effects

Optional character vector of effects to plot. If NULL (the default), all main effects and interactions in the formula are detected automatically.

type

Scale of predictions. One of "response" (outcome scale with observation-process noise), "link" (link-scale linear predictor), "expected" (E[Y]; default), or one of the family-specific scales handled by predict.mvgam(): "variance", "latent_state", "detection". For occ() and nmix(), "latent_state" plots the state apart from detection: the probability of occupancy psi, or the expected abundance lambda. "detection" plots the detection probability p.

points

Logical or numeric. If TRUE (or a non-zero alpha between 0 and 1), raw observations are overlaid on the plot. The overlay applies where the drawn quantity shares the observations' scale, which covers type = "response" and type = "expected".

rug

Logical. If TRUE, rug tick marks are drawn along the axes, on the same scales the points overlay applies to.

process_error

Logical. Passed to plot_predictions() / get_predict.mvgam. With the default FALSE the trend contributes its deterministic submodel. The panel then shows the covariate effect with the latent process held out. TRUE integrates over the trend's dynamics, which widens the band by the latent state's own spread.

series

Which series the panels show. NULL (the default) draws one panel per effect at the reference series, as brms does for a grouping factor. A factor model whose trend_formula uses lv_axis() gives each series its own effect. NULL then draws a panel per series. "all" draws a panel per series for any model. A single integer or character value picks one series and filters the prediction grid to its observations.

resp

Character specifying which response variable for multivariate models. NULL (default) returns predictions for all responses.

...

Ignored.

plot

Logical. If TRUE (default), draws each plot; otherwise returns the list invisibly so callers can post-process.

ask

Logical. If TRUE, prompts before each new plot.

row.names, optional

Ignored.

Value

An object of class mvgam_conditional_effects: a named list with one ggplot per effect, drawn by the plot and print methods.

Invisibly, a flat named list of ggplot objects, as brms::conditional_effects() plots return one. A multivariate fit's panels are named <response>.<effect>, response by response.

References

Arel-Bundock, V., Greifer, N. and Heiss, A. (2024). How to interpret statistical models using marginaleffects for R and Python. Journal of Statistical Software, 111(9):1-32. doi:10.18637/jss.v111.i09

See also

marginaleffects::predictions() returns the plotted values as a data frame. marginaleffects::avg_slopes() and marginaleffects::avg_comparisons() summarise effects as numbers. posterior_epred.mvgam() computes the expected values the panels draw. pp_check.mvgam() checks the fit against the data. The overview vignette interprets effects in both formulas.

Other predictions: conditional_smooths.mvgam(), fitted.mvgam(), hindcast.mvgam(), posterior_epred.mvgam(), posterior_linpred.mvgam(), posterior_predict.mvgam(), posterior_smooths.mvgam(), predict.mvgam(), predictive_error.mvgam(), predictive_interval.mvgam()

Author

Nicholas J Clark

Examples

# \dontrun{
set.seed(13)
simdat <- sim_mvgam(family = poisson(), n_series = 1L,
                     n_timepoints = 120L, trend_model = AR())
mod <- mvgam(y ~ s(x), trend_formula = ~ AR(p = 1),
              data    = simdat$data_train,
              family  = poisson(),
              chains  = 2, silent = 2)
#> Warning: 9 of 2000 (0.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.

# The effect of x on the expected count, with the observations
conditional_effects(mod, points = TRUE)


# The same effect on the log link scale
conditional_effects(mod, type = "link")


# The average slope of the expected count with respect to x
marginaleffects::avg_slopes(mod, variables = "x", type = "expected")
#> 
#>  Estimate 2.5 % 97.5 %
#>     -1.64  -3.8 0.0399
#> 
#> Term: x
#> Type: expected
#> Comparison: dY/dX
#> 

# Next: marginaleffects::plot_predictions() draws custom effect
# displays, such as one covariate conditional on another
# }
